entries.reason: Screened 70 of 70 carriers. childHint 'A reason has to be given, not guessed. Ask what the text says about why.' describes a move (check the stated reason against the guessed one) and asserts no feature of the item; it holds on every carrier whose option supplies a reason, which is all the correctly filed ones. Both sentences are within 16 words, end on a full stop, British English, actionable in a silent test. Description 'Attributes a plausible motive the text never supports.' is true of every correctly filed carrier. The carriers listed below invent something other than a motive (an action, a blame, an opinion, a condition, a vocabulary sense); that is an item filing fault, not an entry fault. Note ENG-007-LP-13 carries the entry with no execution recorded.

assertionClauses.clause: Ask what the text says about why.
assertionClauses.note: A move, not a feature claim. It presupposes the option supplies a reason, which fails only on the misfiled carriers below.

entries.reason: R586's flagged clause IS STILL THERE: the exported childHint reads 'Two people are being described. Check which one each detail belongs to.' Screened 44 of 44 carriers (R586 cited 43). On my reading the clause is false on 20 of 44: the detail moves between things (boat, house, flame, knocker, sand, hat, time), between a person and a group, among three people, or within one person at the wrong value. This does not match R586's 26; the difference is in borderline calls I counted as TRUE: WIW-17 (Mole and Rat, animal characters), LW-05 (Meg and Beth swapped), SM-12 (Nan and him). The second sentence describes a move and survives every carrier once it covers things as well as people. The description's 'one character's described attribute' is likewise false where the holder is an object and the 'wrong value' clause does not cover it. Residual: on ENG-004-AGG-04 (boy vs girl, one person) neither the old nor the proposed hint speaks to the wrong-value half.

assertionClauses.count: 11 of 44 (holder is an object or abstraction, not covered by the 'wrong value' clause)

entries.reason: Revised on the coordinator's ruling: keep Annie's meaning (a cause that happens LATER in the passage than the effect asked about) and refile, rather than widen the entry. Screened 40 of 40. The childHint 'Check what happened first, and what the question asks for.' stays as it is; it passes both passes. The description's only fault on the correctly filed carriers is the stale closing sentence 'Currently split across ...', a proposal-time note that is no longer true now the entry is active; that is the one transform. 11 of 40 carriers make the later-cause mistake: ENG-005-BB-06, ENG-006-TM-05, ENG-008-RC-06, ENG-008-RC-09, ENG-010-JE-03, ENG-010-JE-05, ENG-013-TI-06, ENG-014-TS-01, ENG-014-TS-05, ENG-014-TS-09, ENG-020-HD-01. 29 of 40 do not and are listed as misfiled: 27 whose stems ask for no cause, plus ENG-019-BV-02 and ENG-020-HD-06, where 'both real' is false. 10 of the 29 are a reversed order of two real events, and NO EXISTING ENTRY covers that; they carry belongsUnder null and need a ruling. The entry is REFUSE only for the stale sentence; the scope stays as approved.

entries.reason: Screened 32 of 32 carriers. The description 'Attributes the right event to the wrong cause or character' has two halves; the childHint 'Ask what exactly made this happen.' serves only the cause half. On 12 of 32 carriers the question is not about what made something happen: the option gives an act, a word or a seeing to the wrong character (who did it, who said it, who was sent). There 'what made this happen' presupposes a cause the item does not ask for and points the child at the wrong check. 'Re-read the moment step by step.' is a move and survives all carriers. Sentences are within 16 words and end on full stops.

assertionClauses.clause: Ask what exactly made this happen.
assertionClauses.count: 12 of 32 (no cause asked for; the error is the wrong character)
